Immigration (Biblical)
im-uh-GRAY-shun
noun (Christian ethics)
The substantive question of how the biblical material on the sojourner / stranger (Hebrew ger) bears on contemporary immigration policy. The biblical material includes commands to love and care for the sojourner (Leviticus 19:33-34), the requirement that the sojourner submit to the law of the land (Leviticus 24:22), and the affirmation of national borders and ordered nations (Acts 17:26; Deuteronomy 32:8).

See also: Immigration (Biblical)

📖 Biblical Definition

The substantive question of how the biblical material on the sojourner / stranger (Hebrew ger) bears on contemporary immigration policy. The biblical material requires substantive balanced reading. (1) Commands to love and care for the sojourner: the Mosaic law commands Israel to love the ger (the resident foreigner who has joined Israel) as themselves, remembering that they were sojourners in Egypt (Leviticus 19:33-34; Deuteronomy 10:18-19); the sojourner is included in the gleaning provisions and the Sabbath rest (Leviticus 19:9-10; Exodus 20:10); the LORD executes justice for the sojourner (Deuteronomy 10:18). (2) The requirement that the sojourner submit to the law of the land: the ger who dwells in Israel is required to keep the same law as the native Israelite (Leviticus 24:22, ye shall have one manner of law, as well for the stranger, as for one of your own country; Exodus 12:48-49, the sojourner who would keep the Passover must be circumcised); the biblical ger is the assimilating sojourner who adopts the religion and law of Israel, not a foreigner maintaining a separate religious-cultural identity. (3) The affirmation of national borders and ordered nations: the LORD has determined the bounds and times of the nations (Acts 17:26; Deuteronomy 32:8); the nations are a substantive part of God's providential ordering (the table of nations in Genesis 10; the diversity of nations gathered in Revelation 7:9); national borders and ordered national life are not contrary to Scripture. The patriarchal-Reformed reader engages the immigration question with substantive balance against two opposing distortions. The progressive distortion uses the love-the-sojourner texts to argue for open borders and the elimination of immigration law; this ignores the assimilation requirement (the biblical ger submits to the law and adopts the religion of the land) and the affirmation of ordered national borders. The nativist distortion ignores the substantive biblical command to love and care for the genuine sojourner. The substantive biblical position: the nation may justly maintain ordered borders and immigration law (Acts 17:26); the sojourner who comes lawfully and assimilates is to be loved and cared for (Leviticus 19:33-34); the substantive concern is ordered, lawful, assimilating immigration under just national governance, not open borders or nativist cruelty.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

How the biblical sojourner / stranger material (Hebrew ger) bears on immigration; commands to love the sojourner (Leviticus 19:33-34), the requirement that the sojourner submit to the law (Leviticus 24:22), and the affirmation of ordered national borders (Acts 17:26); held against both open-borders and nativist distortions.

IMMIGRATION (BIBLICAL), n. (Christian ethics) How the biblical sojourner/stranger material (ger) bears on immigration policy. (1) Commands to love and care for the sojourner (Leviticus 19:33-34; Deuteronomy 10:18-19; gleaning and Sabbath inclusion). (2) Requirement that the sojourner submit to the law of the land (Leviticus 24:22, one manner of law; Exodus 12:48-49, circumcision to keep Passover) — the biblical ger is the assimilating sojourner who adopts the religion and law of Israel. (3) Affirmation of ordered national borders (Acts 17:26; Deuteronomy 32:8; Genesis 10 table of nations). Held against progressive open-borders distortion (ignores assimilation and borders) and nativist distortion (ignores the command to love the sojourner). Position: ordered, lawful, assimilating immigration under just governance.

📖 Key Scripture

Leviticus 19:33-34 — "And if a stranger sojourn with thee in your land, ye shall not vex him. But the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God."

Leviticus 24:22 — "Ye shall have one manner of law, as well for the stranger, as for one of your own country: for I am the LORD your God."

Acts 17:26 — "And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation."

Exodus 12:48-49 — "And when a stranger shall sojourn with thee, and will keep the passover to the LORD, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it... One law shall be to him that is homeborn, and unto the stranger that sojourneth among you."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The biblical immigration material is held against two distortions: the progressive open-borders reading (which ignores assimilation and ordered borders) and the nativist reading (which ignores the command to love the genuine sojourner).

expand to see more

The biblical immigration material requires substantive balanced reading against two opposing distortions. The progressive distortion uses the love-the-sojourner texts (Leviticus 19:33-34; Deuteronomy 10:18-19) to argue for open borders, the elimination of immigration law, and the moral obligation to admit all who wish to come. This reading ignores two substantive biblical realities: the biblical ger is the assimilating sojourner who submits to the law of the land and adopts the religion of Israel (Leviticus 24:22; Exodus 12:48-49 — the foreigner who would keep the Passover must be circumcised and join the covenant people), not a foreigner maintaining a separate religious-cultural identity; and the LORD has determined the ordered bounds and times of the nations (Acts 17:26; Deuteronomy 32:8), affirming national borders and ordered national life as part of His providential ordering. The nativist distortion ignores the substantive biblical command to love and care for the genuine sojourner who comes lawfully (Leviticus 19:33-34, the sojourner to be loved as oneself). The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive balanced position: the nation may justly maintain ordered borders and immigration law (Acts 17:26); the sojourner who comes lawfully and assimilates (adopting the law, language, and ideally the religion of the land) is to be loved and cared for; the substantive concern is ordered, lawful, assimilating immigration under just national governance — neither open borders (which dissolves the nation and ignores assimilation) nor nativist cruelty (which ignores the command to love the genuine sojourner).

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Sojourner/stranger material (ger); love the sojourner (Leviticus 19:33-34); sojourner submits to the law (Leviticus 24:22); ordered national borders (Acts 17:26); held against open-borders and nativist distortions.
